title: How to Reduce Taxes on Investment Income in Retirement
description: Managing Capital Gains, Dividends, and Ordinary Income brackets.
content:
Retirees often face a 'Tax Surprise.' They assume their tax rate will be lower in retirement, but between RMDs, taxable Social Security, and capital gains, their effective rate can actually rise. However, unlike W-2 employees, retirees have control over *type* of income they generate. By strategically choosing which accounts to pull from and which assets to hold, you can shift income from the 'Ordinary' bucket (high tax) to the 'Capital Gains' bucket (low tax) or the 'Roth' bucket (zero tax).

Key Takeaways

  • Asset Location: Keep bonds (Ordinary Income) in IRAs. Keep stocks (Capital Gains) in Brokerage. This simple sort minimizes your annual tax bill.
  • The 0% Capital Gains Bracket: If your taxable income is under ~$94,000 (Married), your Long-Term Capital Gains rate is 0%. You can sell stock for a huge profit and pay the IRS nothing.
  • Tax-Loss Harvesting: In retirement, use losses to offset gains. If you sell a winner to live on, sell a loser to cancel out the tax. Up to $3,000 of excess loss can deduct against your pension income.
  • Municipal Bonds: For high-income retirees (pushing into 32% brackets), switching taxable bonds to Muni bonds (Tax-Free) increases after-tax yield.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The 'Net Investment Income Tax' (NIIT) is a 3.8% surtax on investment income for high earners (AGI > $250k couple). Managing your AGI to stay below this line saves you 3.8% on every dollar of investment profit.

The Tax Efficiency Ladder

Prioritize income sources by tax rate.

Tier 1: Tax-Free (The Best)

  • Roth IRA Withdrawals: $0 Tax.
  • HSA Withdrawals (Medical): $0 Tax.
  • Municipal Bond Interest: $0 Federal Tax.
  • Return of Principal: Selling stock basis. $0 Tax.

Tier 2: Preferred Rates (0% / 15% / 20%)

  • Long-Term Capital Gains: Profits on stocks held >1 year.
  • Qualified Dividends: Most US stock dividends.
  • Strategy: Fill your brackets with this income after Ordinary Income.

Tier 3: Ordinary Income (10% - 37%)

  • Traditional IRA/401k Withdrawals.
  • Pension Income.
  • Bond Interest.
  • REIT Dividends.
  • Strategy: Minimize this. It triggers higher taxes on Social Security.

Harvesting Gains at 0%

  1. Calculate 'Room': If your Pension + SS = $50,000, and the 0% Capital Gains limit is $94,000, you have $44,000 of 'room'.
  2. Execute Sale: Sell $44,000 of winners in your brokerage account.
    Tax Bill: $0.
  3. Reset Basis: Immediately buy back the same stock (or similar). You have now 'stepped up' your cost basis for free, reducing future taxes.
  4. Watch State Tax: Federal capital gains might be 0%, but your state might still tax it as income (e.g., CA/NY). Check local laws.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does this affect Medicare?

Yes. Capital Gains increase your AGI, which determines IRMAA (Medicare Surcharges). Even if the tax rate is 0%, the income counts for Medicare formulas.

What is specific ID?

When selling, tell your broker to sell 'Specific Shares' (the ones with the highest cost basis). This lowers the realized gain, lowering the tax.

Should I avoid dividends?

In a taxable account, yes, high dividends force you to pay tax annually. Growth stocks (buybacks) let you defer tax until you sell. It is more efficient.
